questions.question: What is the primary goal of Problem Management?

options.text: To restore service as quickly as possible
To identify the root cause and prevent future incidents
To approve and implement changes
To manage the service catalog

explanation.correct: Problem Management aims to identify the root cause of incidents, find feasible workarounds, and implement permanent solutions that prevent future occurrences. Unlike Incident Management which focuses on quick restoration, Problem Management focuses on long-term prevention.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Quick service restoration is the goal of Incident Management, not Problem Management
Approving and implementing changes is the responsibility of Change Management
Service Catalog management is separate from Problem Management

source.excerpt: Our goal in Problem Management is to identify the root cause of incidents, find feasible workarounds, and implement permanent solutions that prevent future occurrences.

questions.question: What is the Known Error Database (KEDB)?

options.text: A list of all open incidents
A repository of problem records designated as known issues
A database of all configuration items
A collection of change requests

explanation.correct: The Known Error Database is a repository of problem records that a company has designated as known issues. These problems can be active (still under investigation) or closed (with a workaround in use instead of a permanent solution).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Open incidents are tracked in the Incident table, not the KEDB
Configuration items are stored in the CMDB, not the KEDB
Change requests have their own table; KEDB is for known problems

source.excerpt: The known error database is a repository of problem records that a company has designated as known issues.

questions.question: What happens when a problem record is assigned and saved?

options.text: The status changes from New to Closed
The status changes from New to Assess
The status remains in New state
The status changes directly to Root Cause Analysis

explanation.correct: After saving the assigned problem, its status changes from New to Assess. The support group property automatically fills the Assignment Group field, and at this point, investigation for similar incidents and duplicates can begin.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Problems don't jump directly to Closed; they go through assessment and investigation
The state changes to Assess upon assignment, not remaining New
Root Cause Analysis comes after the Assess state

source.excerpt: After saving the assigned problem, its status changes from new to assess.

questions.question: Which two questions should Root Cause Analysis focus on answering? (Select two)

options.text: What happened?
Who is responsible?
Why did it happen?
How much did it cost?

explanation.correct: During root cause analysis, the focus should be on finding answers to two key questions: What happened? And Why did it happen? This systematic approach helps identify underlying causes rather than just treating symptoms.

wrongAnswers.explanation: RCA focuses on causes, not blame assignment
Cost analysis is separate from root cause analysis

source.excerpt: During the root-cause analysis, we should focus on finding answers to two key questions-- what happened? And why did it happen?

questions.question: Which role is the only one that can reopen a problem record?

options.text: problem_admin
problem_task_analyst
problem_manager
itil

explanation.correct: The problem_manager role enables a user to create and update problems, problem tasks, and related records. This user can also administer problem properties, and this is the only role that can reopen a problem record.

wrongAnswers.explanation: problem_admin can create, update, and delete problems but cannot reopen them
problem_task_analyst can only create and update problem tasks, not reopen problems
The ITIL role provides general capabilities but not problem reopening

source.excerpt: This user can also administer problem properties, and this is the only role that could reopen a problem record. So someone serving as a manager would need this role.

questions.question: How can the problem owner share a workaround with related incidents?

options.text: By manually updating each incident record
By clicking 'Communicate Workaround' which updates the Additional Comments field
By sending a separate email to each incident caller
By closing all related incidents automatically

explanation.correct: The problem owner can communicate the workaround to affected incidents by clicking the appropriate link, which places the workaround in the Additional Comments field on related incidents so callers and anyone on the watch list receive the update.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual updates aren't necessary; the Communicate function automates this
The system handles notification through the incident's Additional Comments field
Communicating a workaround doesn't automatically close incidents

source.excerpt: We can communicate the workaround and place it within the additional comments field on any related incident so that the caller or anyone on the watch list or anyone assigned to the incident would receive that update.

questions.question: A workaround has been implemented for a problem, but no permanent solution will be pursued due to cost. What happens to the problem record?

options.text: It is deleted from the system
It is marked Resolved but remains in the Known Error Database
It stays in the Fix In Progress state indefinitely
It is automatically converted to a change request

explanation.correct: When a workaround is found satisfactory and no permanent solution is implemented, the issue record will still be listed in the Known Error Database despite being marked as Resolved. This ensures the workaround information remains accessible.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Problems are not deleted; they remain for historical reference in the KEDB
The problem can be resolved even without a permanent fix if a workaround suffices
Problems aren't automatically converted; change requests are created when needed

source.excerpt: In cases where the workaround was found to be satisfactory and no permanent solution was implemented, the issue record will still be listed in the known error database despite being marked as resolved.

questions.question: What are the three lifecycle stages in Problem Management?

options.text: Create, Approve, Implement
Detection and Logging, Investigation and Diagnosis, Resolution and Closure
New, In Progress, Closed
Assess, Authorize, Review

explanation.correct: The lifecycle for managing problems starts with Detection and Logging, then moves into Investigation and Diagnosis, and finally concludes with Resolution and Closure.

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are change management stages, not problem management
These are generic task states, not the Problem Management lifecycle stages
These are change management authorization stages

source.excerpt: The life cycle for managing problems starts with detecting and logging them, then moving into investigation and diagnosis, and finally concluding with resolution and closure.

questions.question: What is the purpose of problem tasks?

options.text: To automatically close related incidents
To seek help from other teams without reassigning the problem
To convert problems into change requests
To notify management of problem status

explanation.correct: If assistance is needed from other teams without reassigning the problem record, problem tasks can be used. The assigned problem owner remains accountable for the problem but can create and assign tasks to seek help with the investigation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Problem tasks don't automatically close incidents
Change requests are created separately from problem tasks
Problem tasks are for investigation work, not status notifications

source.excerpt: If you require assistance from other teams or individuals without reassigning the problem record, you can use problem tasks. This way, the assigned problem owner remains accountable for the entire problem record but can still create and assign tasks to seek help with the investigation.

questions.question: When creating a change request from a problem form, which fields are copied to the change request?

options.text: Only the problem number
Short description, description, configuration item, and priority
Only the assignee information
All fields including work notes

explanation.correct: When creating a change request from the problem form, certain fields are copied including the short description, description, configuration item, and priority. This helps ensure consistency between the problem and related change.

wrongAnswers.explanation: More than just the problem number is copied to the change request
Key problem details are copied, not just assignee information
Not all fields are copied; specific relevant fields are transferred

source.excerpt: When creating the change request form, the problem form, some fields are copied from the problem record to the change request. For example, the short description, the description, the configuration item, as well as the priority.

questions.question: Which role is required to create and update problem tasks in ServiceNow?

options.text: problem_admin
problem_manager
problem_task_analyst
itil

explanation.correct: The problem_task_analyst role enables a user to create and update problem tasks. This role is typically assigned to anyone serving in the support group. The problem_admin role can manage problems and tasks, while problem_manager can also administer properties and reopen problems.

wrongAnswers.explanation: problem_admin can create, update, and delete problems, problem tasks, and related records — it has broader access than needed just for tasks.
problem_manager handles properties and can reopen problem records, but problem_task_analyst is the specific role for creating/updating tasks.
The ITIL role is used for incident and change management access, not specifically for problem tasks.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Detection and Logging

source.excerpt: We also have the problem_task_analyst role, enabling a user with this specific role to create an update problem tasks.

questions.question: Which two types of changes can be created from a problem record when implementing a permanent solution? (Choose two.)

options.text: Normal change
Standard change
Emergency change
Automated change

explanation.correct: When implementing a permanent solution or workaround from a problem, only normal changes and emergency changes are applicable. Standard changes are pre-approved repeatable processes and not triggered from problem resolution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Standard changes are pre-approved and repeatable. Problem-driven changes require assessment and are not pre-approved.
Automated change is not a valid change type in ServiceNow ITSM. The three types are Normal, Standard, and Emergency.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Investigation and Resolution

source.excerpt: Out of the three types of changes, only emergency changes and normal changes are applicable in such scenarios.

questions.question: A problem has been resolved with only a workaround and no permanent solution was implemented. What is the status of this problem in the Known Error Database?

options.text: It is removed from the Known Error Database
It remains listed in the Known Error Database despite being marked as resolved
It is moved to a separate archive database
It is automatically converted to a change request

explanation.correct: When a workaround is deemed satisfactory and no permanent solution is implemented, the issue record remains in the Known Error Database even though the problem is marked as resolved. This ensures future incidents can reference the workaround.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Resolved problems with workarounds stay in the KEDB to help with future incident resolution.
There is no separate archive database. The KEDB maintains both active and closed known errors.
A workaround-only resolution does not trigger an automatic change request.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Investigation and Resolution

source.excerpt: The issue record will still be listed in the known error database despite being marked as resolved.

questions.question: What is the unique record prefix for problem tasks in ServiceNow?

options.text: PRB
PTASK
PT
PROB

explanation.correct: Problem tasks are identified by their unique PTASK number. Problems themselves use the PRB prefix, but problem tasks specifically use PTASK.

wrongAnswers.explanation: PRB is the prefix for problem records, not problem tasks.
PT is not a valid ServiceNow record prefix.
PROB is not a valid ServiceNow record prefix. Problems use PRB.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Investigation and Resolution

source.excerpt: You can refer to its unique PTASK number located in the top-left corner of the problem task form.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to access the Known Error Database in ServiceNow?

options.text: Problem > Known Errors module
Knowledge Home page > Known Error Knowledge Base
Incident form > Related Links > Known Errors
Related Links on the Problem form (Create Known Error Article)

explanation.correct: The Known Error Database can be accessed through the Problem Known Errors module and the Knowledge Home page's Known Error Knowledge Base. Known error articles can also be generated from the Problem form's related links. Accessing it directly from the Incident form's Related Links is not a standard method.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Problem Known Errors module is a valid way to access the KEDB.
The Known Error Knowledge Base on the Knowledge Home page is a valid access point.
Creating known error articles from the Problem form's related links is a valid method.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Detection and Logging

source.excerpt: To access the known error database, navigate to the Problem Known Errors module or the Known Error Knowledge Base on the Knowledge Home page.

questions.question: What information is automatically transferred when creating a Known Error article from the Problem form?

options.text: Short description, workarounds, and call notes
Assignment group, priority, and configuration item
Related incidents, change requests, and SLA data
Root cause analysis results and implementation timeline

explanation.correct: When creating a Known Error article from the Problem form, the problem's brief description, workarounds, and call notes are automatically transferred to the article. This ensures relevant troubleshooting information is available.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment group, priority, and CI are operational fields — they are not transferred to the knowledge article.
Related records and SLA data are not part of the known error article content.
RCA results and timelines are not automatically included in the known error article.

references: ITSM Fundamentals course - Problem Management Detection and Logging

source.excerpt: All relevant information, such as the Problem's brief description, workarounds, and call notes will automatically be transferred to the article.
